clue.text: Staff enabling standards to be raised

definitions.text: Staff enabling standards to be raised

parts.words: Staff enabling standards to be raised
parts.note: standards are flags, and a staff is the tall pole that lets them be hoisted aloft

explanation.surface: Employees who help lift standards at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' and 'standards' read like workers and quality levels; here a staff is a pole and standards are banners.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a tall staff from which flags (standards) are hoisted.

clue.text: Extremely funny performer put through the mill

indicators.note: put through means one piece is driven into the middle of another
extremely picks the first and last letters of funny

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A comic entertainer is given a rough time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put through the mill' looks like one idiom, but 'mill' alone is the definition; ACTOR goes between F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a works or plant where goods are manufactured.

clue.text: A party song and dance

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A celebration with music and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is an idiom for a fuss, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Before training at Barts, I'm replaced unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters land in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A student is swapped out before starting at a London hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Barts is St Bartholomew's, a London teaching hospital; the anagram of I'M REPLACED gives the word for studies preceding medical school.
explanation.definitionFit: Premedical study is the preparatory course taken before entering medical training.

clue.text: Party member with yen to oversee a whole country

parts.note: a Lib is a member of the Liberal party
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A political member with money controls a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to oversee' places Y above A.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: Given dream job, journalist congratulated

parts.note: a plum is a highly desirable job
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is praised after landing an ideal post.
explanation.walkthrough: To plume oneself is to congratulate or pride oneself, a sense taken from a bird preening its feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumed (oneself) is an old idiom for preened or self-congratulated, as a bird preens its feathers.

clue.text: To satisfy desire for water head off here?

definitions.text: To satisfy desire for water head off here?

indicators.note: the head of the word is cut off, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: to slake is to quench thirst

explanation.surface: Is this where people go to quench their thirst?
explanation.walkthrough: SLAKE without its first letter; the whole clue also suggests where you would go to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A large body of fresh water, the sort of place one might head to drink.

clue.text: Empty dining area with a fireplace installed

indicators.note: installed means put inside, so the fireplace goes into the dining area

parts.note: a mess is where service personnel eat
an is the form of a
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth

explanation.surface: A vacant restaurant fitted with a new hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed' is the container signal; 'a' is read as the article's other form. An ingle is an old word for a hearth, as in inglenook.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty words lack substance or sense, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Tried to bring new order to city

indicators.note: bring new order says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city was the target of an attempted reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michigan car-making centre is an example of a city.

clue.text: Observer proprietor supporting British enterprise originally

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the others
originally takes the first letter of enterprise

parts.note: a holder is an owner

explanation.surface: The owner of a newspaper backs British business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' hints at the newspaper, but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who sees or watches, an observer.

clue.text: All right during school holiday to refrain from eating hot meal

indicators.note: during places one item within the span of another, so OK goes inside

parts.note: a coed is a co-educational school
OK means all right
a break is a short holiday from school
to fast is to go without food

explanation.surface: A pupil on vacation may skip eating a cooked meal.
explanation.walkthrough: COED, a mixed school, is mainly American usage; a British full English of eggs and bacon is the classic example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A full plate of fried eggs, bacon and sausages served in the morning is a typical hot meal.

clue.text: A gent who gets drunk working perhaps should go here?

definitions.text: A gent who gets drunk working perhaps should go here?

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: a drunk staggers, so the letters of the phrase lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy gentleman at work ought perhaps to take the pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets drunk' is the anagram signal. The whole clue also says where a drinker should go, since the idiom means abstaining from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the wagon is the idiom for giving up alcohol, the place a drinker is urged to go.

clue.text: Style of painting intended, say, to portray nature

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment mixed in egg

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: An artist's chosen technique depicts the outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's temperament is their basic nature or disposition.

clue.text: Put removable cover round swimming pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover that comes off
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An instruction to fit a detachable cover around a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool, a common British term.

clue.text: Providers of such entertainment work hand in glove

definitions.text: Providers of such entertainment work hand in glove

parts.words: Providers of such entertainment work hand in glove
parts.note: hand in glove usually means in close cooperation, but here the performers literally put a hand inside a glove figure

explanation.surface: Entertainers cooperate closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand in glove' reads as close collaboration but is literal: glove puppets.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove-puppet performance is put on by people whose hands are inside the figures.

clue.text: Going on laborious march? You can't finish —— whizz back in car

indicators.note: the word You is not allowed to complete itself, so its last letter goes
in sets one piece within the letters of another

parts.note: MG is a classic British sports car make

indicators.note: back means the word for whizz is turned around

parts.note: to nip is to go quickly

explanation.surface: Is this a hard trek? You stall, so speed back in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIP into PIN, placed in MG. To yomp is British military slang for marching with heavy kit over rough ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Yomping is soldiers' slang for a laborious, heavily loaded march across country.

clue.text: Gallivant with a Frenchman, the swine

definitions.note: the word is an adjective, defined by the pigs it describes

parts.note: to gad is to gallivant
Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Someone runs around with a French man, the brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the swine' looks like an insult; it alludes to the Gospel herd that rushed headlong into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel herd of pigs possessed by demons came from Gadara, giving the adjective for that herd.

clue.text: Dirt initially sticking to carpet? Acquire protective floor covering

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word Dirt

parts.note: a rug is a small carpet
to get is to acquire

explanation.surface: Muck sticks to a carpet, so buy a protective mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drugget is a coarse cloth laid over a carpet or floor to protect it.

clue.text: Help with homework settled in advance

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework
aid means help

explanation.surface: Assistance with schoolwork has already been paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill paid ahead of time has been settled in advance, the plain synonym.

clue.text: A sleep round about one: that will cure anything

indicators.note: about means surrounding the next piece
round turns the two words back to front

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A nap at around one o'clock fixes everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns both A and the sleep word back to front; 'about' then wraps that run round the card word, which sits just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal remedy is something supposed to cure every ill.

clue.text: Curb on media

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a memo heading
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A restriction placed on the news outlets.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb feelings is to hold them down, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drugs one abandoned set aside for redistribution

indicators.note: abandoned says the one is left out of the pool of letters
for redistribution means the remaining letters are shared out in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Medicines once discarded are set aside to hand out again.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I from SET ASIDE and rearrange SETASDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To drug someone is to calm them with medication, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Refusal to take a horse? He took two

parts.note: no is a refusal
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse refuses a jump; someone else took a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks literal but is drug slang for heroin, H. The definition alludes to the ark, which took the animals in two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical ark-builder took every animal aboard in pairs, two of each kind.

clue.text: Made enquiries about tax before one's sold off

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the enquiring word goes around the rest

parts.note: pried means made nosy enquiries

indicators.note: before puts the tax ahead of the next piece

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
one is I, and one's is read as I'S

explanation.surface: Someone asked questions about a tax before it was sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A state industry that has been privatised was sold off to private buyers.

clue.text: Item of kit on display before a match

parts.note: a vest is part of sports kit

explanation.surface: A sportswear garment is shown before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a game, but a vesta is a short wooden match.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesta is an old name for a short friction match for lighting things.

clue.text: Decrease in strength

definitions.meaning: read as de-crease: to remove creases from cloth
the metal stands for firmness, as in a will of steel

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing fabric de-creases it; the hard metal is a byword for strength.

clue.text: Well-trained actor: he learns to prepare for speech

indicators.note: the letters are drilled and trained into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A properly schooled performer learns how to get ready to deliver lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is ACTOR HE LEARNS TO, fifteen letters; 'Well-trained' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Coughing slightly before talking is how a speaker readies the voice, so it means getting ready to speak.

clue.text: Row among skateboarders

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the word

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out among young skaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but is the pole used to row a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To oar a boat is an old verb meaning to propel it with blades, so it can stand for row.

clue.text: Escort for minister

definitions.meaning: to escort someone is to accompany or wait on them
to minister is to wait on or look after someone

explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to escort them; to tend to someone's needs is to minister to them.

clue.text: On evenly cut grass, cultivates plant

indicators.note: removing the even-numbered letters of grass leaves the odd ones

parts.note: to work land is to cultivate it

explanation.surface: Someone tends a lawn with alternate strips mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly cut' removes the second and fourth letters of the grass word; 'On' is read as a link putting the cultivating word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant can be an industrial facility, and this one makes fuel from coal.
